Resolve the common GPU type for one column across a bind/set operation

Source: R/bind.R
resolve_common_col_type.Rd

The type-compatibility ladder shared by check_set_op_compatible() (R/sets.R) and bind_rows()'s compute_unified_schema(), so the set-op verbs and bind_rows() use EXACTLY one promotion rule. A numeric column against a character column of the same name is not coerced to STRING: as in real dplyr (vctrs::vec_ptype2()-backed bind_rows()), it's a hard vctrs_error_incompatible_type, see abort_bind_rows_incompatible() below.

Usage

resolve_common_col_type(
  tx,
  ty,
  fx = FALSE,
  fy = FALSE,
  lvls_x = NULL,
  lvls_y = NULL
)

Arguments

tx, ty

GPU type strings for the two occurrences of this column (unname()d already by the caller)

fx, fy

Logical: is this occurrence DICTIONARY32 (a factor)?

lvls_x, lvls_y

Level vectors for tx/ty when fx/fy is TRUE (NULL otherwise)

Value

A list with $ok (logical) and, when TRUE, $type (promoted type string) and $factor_levels (level vector, or NULL when the result isn't DICTIONARY32)

Details

Four cases, all pinned via oracle-verified dplyr/vctrs behavior:

  • Both factor (DICTIONARY32): union of both level sets (or a no-op if identical) – vctrs::vec_c(factor, factor)'s contract.

  • Exactly one factor, the other STRING: decodes to STRING (dplyr's factor + character -> character contract). Exactly one factor, the other anything else (numeric, timestamp, ...): a hard incompatibility ($ok = FALSE) – real vctrs::vec_ptype2() refuses this too.

  • Identical types: a no-op.

  • Both in the numeric ladder (BOOL8 < INT32 < INT64 < FLOAT64, except that INT64 (integer64) and FLOAT64 have no common type) or both in the timestamp ladder (TIMESTAMP_DAYS < ... < TIMESTAMP_NANOSECONDS): promotes to the wider member. The timestamp cast (Date <-> POSIXct, etc.) is native (gpu_cast_column(), src/ops_bind.cpp, handles the TIMESTAMP_* targets), so this ladder is native for both callers.

  • Anything else (e.g. numeric vs. character, factor vs. numeric, numeric vs. timestamp): $ok = FALSE – the caller reports its own verb-specific incompatibility error (sets.R's "xandy are not compatible." bulleted form vs. bind.R's vctrs-style "Can't combine ..."form, seeabort_bind_rows_incompatible()`).
